To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cell motility can be triggered by the stochastic detachment of adhesive complexes at one side of a cell, 2) the stochastic detachment of adhesions is a generic phenomenon that occurs independently of cell type or cell shape, 3) a theoretical model suggests that the stochastic detachment of cell adhesives can be sufficient for the initiation of cell motility in the absence of a complex self organizing mechanism.
cell adhesion dynamics can trigger spontaneous symmetry breaking and cell migration on 1D microstructures.

cell motility in a complex 1D in vivo like environment can emerge spontaneously by stochastic adhesion dynamics, without prior polarity of cytoskeleton elements, and that the resulting cell polarization is sufficient to drive directional cell migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question in cell motility: what are the minimal requirements for a cell to migrate?
the initiation of directional migration in the absence of prior polarity and provides a new framework to study cell migration and its underlying mechanics in one dimensional microenvironments.
the spatiotemporally resolved quantification and modeling of the initiation of cell motility in a one dimensional environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the initiation of cell migration is a stochastic process that is driven by cell contractility, and that cell motility can be established in 1D by the stochastic stick-slip dynamics of cell adhesive contacts.
stick slip behavior is sufficient for the initiation of directional migration in 1D.
stick slip dynamics of adhesions can trigger cell migration on one dimensional lines in a generic manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stochastic stick-slip behavior of cell adhesins is the key to the initiation of cell migration in the absence of a pre established front rear polarity.
stick slip dynamics of adhesions is a generic mechanism to initiate migration in 1D.
the stochastic stick slip behavior of cell-substrate adhesions, which can be triggered by cell contractility alone, can be sufficient to trigger cell migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell motility can emerge from a simple mechanical system that is driven by contractility and adhesion dynamics.
stick slip dynamics of adhesions are a generic feature of cell motility and are sufficient to trigger directional cell motility.

cell motility can be triggered by the stochastic stick-slip dynamics of adhesive contacts and that the emergence of front rear polarity is not dependent on pre established polarity of the cytoskeleton.
